paragraphs.text: Each guide does one task on one real text. Six show the input, the same call in Rust, Python and the command line, and what matra prints; the three calls print the same result, and CI runs all three and compares what they print with the page. The seventh has no command-line call, because the CLI has no command for it.

Install matra the way you mean to use it: the library, the CLI, or the Python package (Install matra). The Rust calls also need serde_json to print, which is the first line of each one: cargo add matra@0.3 serde_json.

Each call reads its input from the directory it runs in, under the file name the page gives. Each page has the command that downloads it. The first call on a machine downloads the English model (about 16 MB), and every later call reads it from disk.
Analyzing a directory as a corpus has no worked example here, because each example pins the output of one input. The CLI, Rust and Python guides cover it.
